title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
event_hint: arXiv publication of CodeGrep retrieval agent
problem: LLM coding agents (Claude Code, OpenHands) spend most of their token budget finding the file to patch, not patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified, a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, with many calls spent on grep, glob, and view_file during repository exploration.
mechanism: CodeGrep is a 14B retrieval agent trained end-to-end with GRPO to issue multi-turn parallel grep/glob/read tool calls and return candidate files to a frozen downstream coding agent. It uses CATM (Code Agent Trajectory Mining) to mine supervision from 67K open-source agent trajectories, and a Git-worktree environment for multi-turn agent RL.

evidence.claim: CodeGrep improves efficiency on SWE-Bench Verified: 15% fewer rounds and 19% fewer tokens on resolved instances while improving resolve rate from 25.8% to 27.0%
evidence.condition: on resolved SWE-Bench Verified instances, downstream agent: OpenHands with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, temperature 0, 100-round max

evidence.claim: Precision threshold for retriever utility: BM25 precision 0.375 degrades agent, Jina 0.445 is neutral, CodeGrep 0.677 crosses threshold for efficiency gain
evidence.condition: precision at which retrieval begins to reduce rollout cost

evidence.claim: Training data from 67,074 open-source OpenHands trajectories using CATM pipeline, yielding 31,977 effective training samples (47.7% retention)
Reward design: applying efficiency signal at advantage layer (v2/v3) reduces KL drift to 0.09-0.15 vs 0.31 for reward layer (v1)
Git-worktree sandbox reduces per-rollout environment setup from minutes to milliseconds, enabling training on single 8x B200 node in ~27 hours

evaluation_context: SWE-Bench Verified (500 instances). Downstream agent: OpenHands (Wang et al., 2024) with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507. Temperature 0, 100-round maximum. Training: single 8x B200 node with LoRA, optimizer offload, and vLLM-colocated rollout. Early-stop at step 897 of planned 2000 steps.
limitations: Evidence pack limited to abstract/intro/early design sections; detailed experimental results tables, error analysis, ablation studies, and explicit limitations sections not visible. Index construction cost, repository update overhead, and real-world deployment constraints not described in visible evidence. Precision-only evaluation may miss recall trade-offs.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to agent acceleration. CodeGrep demonstrates a clean retrieval-based acceleration approach: training a smaller retrieval agent via RL to reduce redundant Read/Grep operations in larger coding agents. Key insights: (1) RL for tool policies works for code retrieval; (2) efficiency signal belongs at advantage layer, not reward layer; (3) retrievers need high precision (~0.68) to be net-positive for downstream agents; (4) Git-worktree environments enable practical multi-turn agent RL. This validates precision-first retrieval acceleration without heavy indexing infrastructure.
